title: The effects of climate change could adversely affect JPMorganChase’s business and operations, both directly and as a result of impacts on its clients and customers.
label: boilerplate
evidence: Both physical risks and transition risks associated with climate change could negatively impact JPMorganChase and its clients and customers.
reason: The text was condensed and some examples were dropped (reputation, regulatory conflicts, data uncertainty), but the company does not say the climate exposure itself shrank.

title: The Company experiences cybersecurity incidents and inadvertent losses and unauthorized access to or releases of confidential information, including personal information.
label: escalated
evidence: The rapid advancement and widespread dissemination of artificial intelligence technologies significantly increases the risks associated with cybersecurity attacks.
reason: The cyberattack exposure is the same, but it is now described as intensifying because of AI-enabled attacks, with systemic risks and a title saying incidents are already occurring.

title: Our indemnification obligation to fund settlement losses of our clients, and in some cases other third parties, exposes us to significant risk of loss and may adversely impact our liquidity.
label: new_exposure
evidence: the Central Bank of Brazil has adopted regulations applicable to payment networks like Visa that impose enhanced prudential requirements
reason: New Brazilian regulation obligates Visa to absorb settlement losses involving Brazilian sellers and raise collateral, a loss source last year's text did not cover.

title: JPMorganChase faces significant legal risks from civil and governmental proceedings, including litigation, investigations and enforcement actions.
label: boilerplate
evidence: including litigation, investigations and enforcement actions
reason: The text is condensed, and the regulatory-investigation detail is folded into a shorter description; the company does not say the exposure shrank, so the substance is unchanged.

title: JPMorganChase’s compliance risk and operating costs could be higher in jurisdictions with less predictable legal, regulatory and judicial frameworks.
label: boilerplate
evidence: leading to lost revenue
reason: Text was condensed and reworded, and the Russia litigation example was dropped without saying the exposure ended; the list of drivers is otherwise unchanged.

title: The issuance of our common stock upon conversion of our Mandatory convertible preferred stock, and the exchange of the Spirit Exchangeable Notes, as well as any other issuances of our common stock, could dilute the interests of our existing shareholders.
label: new_exposure
evidence: We may also issue shares of our common stock upon the exchange of the $230 million of 3.250% Exchangeable Notes
reason: This year adds a new dilution source, the Spirit Exchangeable Notes assumed in the acquisition, which last year's text did not cover; the completed merger share issuance was dropped.

title: Other digital safety abuses
label: new_exposure
evidence: certain AI technologies, including conversational or emotionally engaging AI systems, may present distinct risks for children and adolescents
reason: Adds new exposures: risks from conversational AI to minors, and age-assurance and parental-control obligations for app stores and operating systems, beyond last year's general content-moderation risk.

title: Delaware law, provisions in our governing documents and our capital structure could make a merger, takeover attempt or change in control difficult.
label: boilerplate
evidence: certain litigation against us or our directors, officers or other employees can only be brought in the state of Delaware or the U.S. federal courts
reason: The added forum-selection clause and the share-class renaming are further governance provisions under the same anti-takeover risk; the exposure is unchanged in substance.

title: We are subject to complex laws, rules, regulations, and political and other actions, including restrictions on the export of our products, which may adversely impact our business.
label: escalated
evidence: we were effectively foreclosed from competing in China's data center computing/compute market
reason: China export-control risk has materialised: a $4.5 billion H20 charge, effective exclusion from China's data center market, and a preliminary Chinese antitrust finding against NVIDIA.

title: Demand for our products and services may be impacted by the status of government and economic incentives supporting the development and adoption of such products.
label: escalated
evidence: recent governmental and regulatory actions have repealed and/or restricted consumer, manufacturing and charging infrastructure tax credits, and certain regulatory credit programs tied to our products
reason: The incentive-loss risk last year described as possible is now stated as having happened, with repealed EV tax credits and OBBBA impacts on costs and demand.

title: JPMorgan Chase & Co. is a holding company and depends on its subsidiaries for funding to make payments on its outstanding securities.
label: boilerplate
evidence: JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. is subject to regulatory restrictions and requirements relating to the dividends that it can pay to the Parent Company
reason: Text is condensed and reworded, dropping the SLR mention; the exposure, its constraints and the bankruptcy consequence are unchanged in substance.

title: Damage to JPMorganChase’s reputation could negatively affect its business, results and prospects.
label: boilerplate
evidence: JPMorganChase’s reputation could be harmed by its decisions to engage or not engage with a client or in a business activity that lead to negative commercial impacts
reason: The text is heavily condensed and drops many listed sources and ESG/activist detail, but it never says the reputational exposure shrank or ended.

title: Declines in U.S., global and regional economic conditions adversely affect our results of operations and financial condition.
label: boilerplate
evidence: plans for our DTC ad-supported services, enhancements, product offerings, pricing structure and price increases and plans for strategic investments
reason: The text was reworded and condensed, dropping the past-impact and recent-inflation examples, with no material change to the described economic exposure.

title: We face risks related to the protection and utilization of our intellectual property that may result in our business and operating results being harmed.
label: de_escalated
evidence: Changes in the law may continue to weaken our ability to prevent the use of patented technology.
reason: This year's text drops two drivers: legal changes weakening patent enforcement, and broad IP licensing through open source engagement. The source-code leak risk is otherwise unchanged.

title: We must minimize disruption caused by production changes, achieve and maintain operational stability and implement productivity improvements to meet customer demand and maintain our profitability.
label: escalated
evidence: planned production rate increases may be delayed or not occur at all if our production health key performance indicators and rate readiness process guided by our Safety Management System do not support increasing production rates or we are unable to obtain FAA concurrence
reason: The same production-rate risk now names specific 737 and 787 targets, FAA concurrence and safety gating, and warns the increases may not happen at all.

title: The Company’s future performance depends in part on support from third-party software developers.
label: new_exposure
evidence: If third-party developers use alternative methods of distribution and payment for their applications and digital content, including direct-to-consumer distribution models, the Company may earn a lower commission
reason: This year adds new loss sources absent last year: App Store commission erosion from alternative distribution, and developer fraud exacerbated by AI, with litigation and regulatory exposure.

title: Competition and technology platforms' business practices:
label: escalated
evidence: in 2025, California and New York passed the Transparency in Frontier Artificial Intelligence Act and the Responsible AI Safety and Education Act, respectively, each of which imposes safety and reporting obligations on developers of frontier models
reason: Last year's text said states 'may move' to regulate AI model development; now such laws have passed, over 1,000 bills were considered, and EU obligations have taken effect.

title: JPMorganChase’s business and operations rely on appropriate staffing and on the competence, trustworthiness, health and safety of employees.
label: boilerplate
evidence: including due to health emergencies or other extraordinary events beyond JPMorganChase’s control
reason: The text was condensed and examples were dropped, such as pandemics and hostilities, but the workforce exposures stay substantively the same and nothing says the risk shrank.

title: Our success depends on our ability to develop, deliver, and maintain competitive cloud-based and AI products and services that achieve broad customer adoption and sustainable revenue growth.
label: boilerplate
evidence: Effectively monetizing our cloud-based and AI products through pricing models that reflect their value while remaining competitive.
reason: The rewrite reorganizes the same execution, adoption, revenue and misuse risks; the new monetization and scrutiny mentions add little substance beyond last year's revenue and competition concerns.

title: Failure to anticipate, adapt to or keep pace with new technologies in the payments industry could harm our business and impact future growth.
label: new_exposure
evidence: Our and our partners’ use of AI depends in part on third-party large language models that we do not control, whose models may generate inaccurate, biased, hallucinated or unexpected outputs
reason: This year adds new loss sources not covered last year: dependence on third-party LLMs, flawed AI outputs causing reputational, regulatory and liability harm, and weak IP protection for AI output.

title: We may not realize the anticipated benefits of mergers, acquisitions, joint ventures/strategic alliances or divestitures.
label: new_exposure
evidence: we are required to provide services to buyers of divested Spirit businesses, including
reason: New obligation to provide services to buyers of divested Spirit businesses, including Airbus, with possible claims. Last year covered only divested businesses' nonperformance under guarantees.

title: Our Commercial Airplanes business depends on our ability to maintain a healthy production system, ensure every airplane in our production system conforms to exacting specifications, achieve planned production rate targets, successfully develop and certify new aircraft or new derivative aircraft, and meet or exceed stringent performance and reliability standards.
label: escalated
evidence: recognized additional reach-forward losses of $4.9 billion and $3.5 billion in 2025 and 2024
reason: The certification-delay risk now cites concrete 777X losses, first delivery slipping to 2027, and 'significant' delays, showing the existing exposure materialising at larger cost.

title: JPMorganChase faces substantial legal and operational risks related to the processing and safeguarding of personal information.
label: boilerplate
evidence: The growing sophistication of technology poses a heightened risk of identity fraud
reason: The text was condensed and reorganized, and AI was generalized to technology; the same exposures remain with no material change in likelihood or scope.

title: A successful cyber attack could cause significant harm to JPMorganChase and its clients and customers.
label: escalated
evidence: JPMorganChase could be required to make significant investments in technology in order to transition effectively to more robust security protections, including quantum-resistant encryption.
reason: Quantum risk was already disclosed; it now adds significant transition costs, a risk that the transition finishes too late, and added vulnerability through slower-adopting third parties.

title: Our fixed-price contracts subject us to losses when we have cost overruns.
label: escalated
evidence: Our fixed-price contracts subject us to losses when we have cost overruns.
reason: Losses are now stated as certain rather than possible, BDS's fixed-price share rose from 54% to 60%, and the risk now covers follow-on production, terminations and cancellations.

title: JPMorganChase’s businesses could be adversely affected if it fails to identify and address operational risks associated with the introduction of or changes to products, services, delivery platforms or technologies.
label: escalated
evidence: has resulted and could in the future result in
reason: The company now says failures to manage operational risk from product and technology changes have already caused harm, and it adds losses from fraudulent transactions as a consequence.

title: Resolving an investigation by a governmental authority could subject JPMorganChase to significant penalties and other repercussions.
label: new_exposure
evidence: be unable to disclose specific information concerning that investigation to the public if such a disclosure would violate JPMorganChase’s obligations under applicable law to maintain confidentiality
reason: New warnings cover a significant investigation the company may be legally unable to disclose, client litigation over compliance actions, and proceedings triggered by other institutions' violations.

title: Government-imposed obligations and/or restrictions on international payments systems may prevent us from competing against providers in certain markets.
label: de_escalated
evidence: approved our Application to Prepare in October 2026, which permits us to begin formal preparations to establish a domestic BCCI
reason: The China licensing exposure is partly resolved: the PBOC approved Visa's preparation stage, though final approval is still uncertain. The rest of the text is largely condensed.

title: Some of our and our suppliers’ workforces are represented by labor unions. Work stoppages by our employees have adversely affected and could continue to adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations and/or cash flows. Future work stoppages by our or our suppliers’ employees could also adversely impact our business.
label: escalated
evidence: During 2025, employees represented by IAM District 837, which represents approximately 3,200 employees at our St. Louis area sites, went out on strike for 101 days
reason: A second strike materialised in 2025, disrupting defense programs; strikes occurred despite tentative agreements, union share rose to 40%, and SPEEA contracts expire in 2026.

title: JPMorganChase's business and operations could be negatively affected by governmental policies that discourage or penalize doing business with certain industries or that require specific business practices.
label: boilerplate
evidence: Governmental policies may differ or conflict across jurisdictions, which could lead to negative consequences for JPMorganChase
reason: This year's text rewords and slightly condenses the same exposures; the omitted text appears truncated, and the company does not say the risk shrank.

title: JPMorganChase’s ability to distribute capital to shareholders, and to support its business activities could be limited if it does not satisfy applicable regulatory capital requirements.
label: new_exposure
evidence: JPMorganChase may use its regulatory capital buffers allowing capital ratios to decline below regulatory requirements, subjecting it to restrictions on capital distributions and discretionary bonus payments
reason: This year adds a new trigger, a deliberate drawdown of capital buffers below requirements, plus a new consequence, restrictions on executive bonuses, neither covered last year.

title: Competition in the financial services industry could lead to negative effects on JPMorganChase’s results of operations.
label: new_exposure
evidence: advocacy by non-banking competitors for exemptions from regulatory requirements could significantly disadvantage traditional financial institutions
reason: This year adds a new source of loss: non-bank competitors winning regulatory exemptions. It also adds regulatory uncertainty over new technologies. Neither was covered last year.

title: We are subject to complex and evolving global regulations that could harm our business and financial results.
label: new_exposure
evidence: require us to maintain additional capital or financial resources
reason: This year adds regulatory capital or financial-resource requirements, plus heavier licensing and supervision for tokenization, push payments and cross-border money movement, none of which last year's text covered.

title: We may be subject to tax examinations or disputes, or changes in tax laws.
label: boilerplate
evidence: including those involving the availability of deductions or credits, transfer pricing, permanent establishment assertions, or indirect and other non-income taxes
reason: The added dispute topics and generic compliance-cost sentence elaborate the existing tax examination and law-change exposure without showing new losses, materialisation, or a larger magnitude.

title: JPMorganChase could incur significant losses arising from concentrations of credit and market risk.
label: new_exposure
evidence: the significant expansion of private credit could worsen losses among non-bank lenders and their borrowers
reason: This year adds private credit expansion and non-bank lender stress spreading to funding markets as a new loss source, which last year's text did not cover.

title: Future operating results depend upon the Company’s ability to obtain components, compute capacity and storage resources in sufficient quantities and on commercially reasonable terms.
label: new_exposure
evidence: The Company’s business, including its artificial intelligence and machine learning offerings, also depends on access to sufficient compute capacity and storage resources.
reason: Adds a new source of loss, compute and storage capacity, third-party cloud providers and data center build-out, beyond the component supply risk covered last year; component constraints also now current.

title: Our ability to adjust to evolving corporate responsibility and sustainability matters and related regulations could adversely affect our business and financial results or negatively impact our reputation.
label: boilerplate
evidence: As governments worldwide continue to adopt CRS-related laws and regulations, we may face additional or more stringent requirements.
reason: The text was reorganized and reworded, with the same regulations, stakeholders and litigation risks as before; the added sentence on more stringent laws restates an existing point.

title: A significant inadequacy in disclosure or financial reporting controls could negatively affect JPMorganChase’s business, operations and reputation.
label: boilerplate
evidence: JPMorganChase’s disclosure and financial reporting controls may not always be effective
reason: The text is condensed and reworded; the same control-weakness exposure and consequences remain, with no new driver and no stated change in likelihood or severity.

title: Climate-related physical and transition risks could disrupt our businesses and adversely affect client activity levels and the creditworthiness of our clients and counterparties, and we are at increased risk of being subject to conflicting legal and regulatory requirements and stakeholder expectations regarding climate-related matters.
label: escalated
evidence: due to increasingly divergent policies and viewpoints regarding climate change, we are at increased risk of being subject to conflicting legal and regulatory requirements
reason: Conflicting climate requirements went from 'potentially conflicting' to an actual, increasing risk now highlighted in the title, outweighing the dropped expectation that climate risks will increase.

title: We may experience outages, disruptions, or capacity constraints if we fail to maintain and operate adequate infrastructure or secure the resources necessary to support it.
label: new_exposure
evidence: we rely on third-party providers, including colocation facilities, leased datacenters, and cloud infrastructure providers, to support portions of our operations.
reason: The company now flags dependence on third-party colocation, leased datacenter and cloud providers whose failures could disrupt services, a counterparty risk last year's text did not address.

title: Failure to meet the evolving needs of our industry and markets may adversely impact our financial results.
label: new_exposure
evidence: We have entered into an intellectual property license arrangement with Groq, Inc., or Groq, that required significant, nonrefundable payments.
reason: New Groq IP license with significant nonrefundable payments introduces a specific counterparty and potential loss on unrecovered costs not covered last year.

title: U.S. HEALTHCARE REGULATION
label: new_exposure
evidence: the FDA's recently adopted policy of disclosing Complete Response Letters for unapproved drug candidates and the attendant risk of disclosure of trade secrets
reason: The FDA's Complete Response Letter disclosure policy, with its risk of exposing trade secrets, is a new source of loss; the enacted OBBBA and the CDC vaccine cuts also escalate existing risks.

title: Failure to effectively manage potential conflicts of interest or to satisfy fiduciary obligations could result in litigation and enforcement actions and cause reputational harm.
label: boilerplate
evidence: provide fiduciary products or services in accordance with applicable law, or
reason: Text was condensed and reworded, merging list items and dropping the client-data bullet, while the conflict-of-interest and fiduciary exposure stays essentially unchanged.

title: Other demand-related factors.
label: new_exposure
evidence: increased demand for artificial intelligence (AI), including the construction and expansion of AI data centers
reason: This year adds two new demand drivers not named last year: AI data center construction and government actions to build strategic reserves.

title: We rely extensively on information and financial systems to process transactions, summarize results and manage our business. Disruptions in our systems could harm our ability to conduct our operations.
label: boilerplate
evidence: catastrophic events noted above in this Item 1A
reason: The list of catastrophic events, utility outages, associate errors and unrest was replaced with a cross-reference; condensing the text does not change the substance of the exposure.

title: Any failure by us to comply with a variety of U.S. and international privacy and consumer protection laws may harm us.
label: boilerplate
evidence: Many other U.S. states have enacted their own distinct privacy laws and regulations
reason: Added mention of other state laws and Asia-Pacific region elaborates already-covered changing U.S. state and international privacy law exposure without materially changing substance.

title: Due to the international nature of the Company's business, geopolitical or economic changes or events, including global tensions and war, could adversely affect our business, results of operations or financial condition.
label: boilerplate
evidence: including data localization laws and restrictions on data transfers
reason: Data localization is a new example of protectionist policies already covered. Other edits generalize the Russia and tariff references and drop 'rising' without changing the substance of the exposure.

title: We derive a significant portion of our revenues from non-U.S. sales and are subject to the risks of doing business in other countries, including those related to tariffs, trade restrictions and government actions.
label: escalated
evidence: in the second quarter of 2025, certain customers in China paused accepting our deliveries in response to ongoing tariff negotiations between the U.S. and China.
reason: The tariff and China trade exposure has materialised: Chinese customers paused deliveries, and the company now warns of broad retaliatory tariffs, lower demand and order terminations.

title: RESPONSIBLE BUSINESS PRACTICES
label: boilerplate
evidence: have differing views on matters perceived to be related to responsible business practices
reason: The exposure is unchanged in substance. Dropping the Rocky Mount tornado example, renaming the title, and softening the stakeholder-pressure wording are rewording and condensing, not a material change.

title: We are exposed to fluctuations in the fair values of our investments and, in some instances, our financial statements incorporate inherently subjective valuation methodologies.
label: boilerplate
evidence: the value of our investments could significantly decline
reason: Text was reordered and clarified, with an added adverb and an accounting note on SBC awards; the investment valuation exposure is substantively unchanged.

title: If we or third parties we rely on sustain cyberattacks or other privacy or data security incidents resulting in disruption to our operations or the misappropriation or disclosure of protected personal information or proprietary or confidential information, we could suffer a loss of revenue and increased costs, negative operational effects, exposure to significant liability, reputational harm and other serious negative consequences.
label: boilerplate
evidence: human error, insider threat, malicious social engineering
reason: Changes are wording tweaks (AI/ML to AI, malicious code phrasing, insider threat added to list); no material change in exposure substance or severity.

title: Our future growth and success are dependent upon demand for our electric vehicles and adoption of autonomous driving solutions.
label: new_exposure
evidence: Upon launching our Robotaxi service in June 2025, we also entered into the autonomous ride-hailing service market, and have plans to mass produce Cybercab
reason: Adds a new business line, the Robotaxi autonomous ride-hailing service and Cybercab, whose success depends on consumer adoption of autonomous driving, which last year's text did not cover.

title: We enter into cost-type contracts, which also carry risks.
label: boilerplate
evidence: each generated approximately 40% of their 2025 revenues from cost-type contracting arrangements
reason: Only the cost-type revenue percentages and year were updated, with small offsetting shifts; the risks and program examples are unchanged.

title: The Company’s business and reputation are impacted by information technology system failures and network disruptions.
label: new_exposure
evidence: the implementation of upgrades or replacements to the Company’s global enterprise resource planning system may result in disruptions, cost overruns or data integrity failures
reason: A new risk source appears: the ERP system implementation, which could cause cost overruns and impair order processing, inventory management and timely financial reporting, none of which last year's text covered.

title: If we do not address evolving consumer product and shopping preferences, our business could suffer.
label: boilerplate
evidence: affordability and changes in consumer lifestyles and spending patterns
reason: The additions on affordability and AI reshaping digital discovery elaborate drivers already covered by pricing pressures and digital evolution, so the exposure is not materially changed.

title: Changes in our credit ratings or macroeconomic conditions may affect our liquidity, increasing borrowing costs and limiting our financing options.
label: escalated
evidence: in 2025, our rating was downgraded by S&P Global Ratings and Moody's Ratings
reason: A second agency, Moody's, has now also downgraded the company's rating, so the credit-rating risk is materialising further than the single S&P downgrade disclosed last year.

title: Access limitations.
label: boilerplate
evidence: through the influence on these processes by well-funded local or international groups opposing the development of these resources
reason: Opposition groups are a new channel for permitting restrictions that were already disclosed; no new source of loss or sign the risk has materialised, so it is essentially rewording.

title: We may not be able to continue to successfully maintain or grow engaging third-party content on our platform or usage of and engagement with applications that integrate with our products.
label: new_exposure
evidence: we may not be successful in obtaining or attracting engaging third-party content
reason: Adds a new exposure: dependence on creators supplying engaging third-party content, which last year's developer-only risk did not cover.

title: Our financial results may be adversely affected if substantial investments in businesses and operations fail to produce expected returns.
label: boilerplate
evidence: or strategic initiative to provide expected returns or profitability, or to do so within anticipated timeframes
reason: Adding strategic initiatives and timing delays slightly broadens the wording, but the exposure is the same investment-return risk and no new source of loss is introduced.

title: Unfavorable media coverage negatively affects our business.
label: escalated
evidence: For example, several bellwether trials in our youth-related litigation matters are scheduled for 2026 and beyond.
reason: Litigation publicity was already covered, but the company now cites scheduled youth-related bellwether trials and younger-user impacts, concrete events that raise the likelihood of negative coverage.

title: JPMorganChase’s results could be materially affected by market fluctuations and significant changes in the valuation of financial instruments.
label: boilerplate
evidence: JPMorganChase’s hedging and other risk management strategies may not always be effective
reason: Wording changes ('may' to 'could', 'disruptions' to 'fluctuations') and removal of the stress-testing sentence are condensation, with no change in substance.

title: Net-zero scenarios.
label: escalated
evidence: Without supportive policies and the innovations they drive, net zero will remain out of reach – for society and for ExxonMobil. Society’s progress continues to lag in these areas.
reason: The company now says society's policy and technology progress is already lagging, making its net-zero ambition harder to reach. That is the same exposure described as currently materialising.

title: Competition laws and new market regulation:
label: escalated
evidence: governments may impose restrictions on the development, deployment, availability, or cross-border access to advanced AI models based on safety, cybersecurity, or national security
reason: The AI regulation risk now adds national-security and cross-border restrictions on advanced models, unpredictable application of existing laws, and new areas such as digital replicas and AI companions.

title: Sellers’ and processors’ continued push to lower acceptance costs and challenge industry practices could harm our business.
label: boilerplate
evidence: sellers and seller-affiliated groups have exerted significant influence in the global payments system to lower acceptance costs
reason: The text is reworded, with slightly stronger phrasing and an expanded EMV acronym, but the exposures, examples and consequences are the same as last year.

title: Changes in technology, in consumer consumption patterns and in how entertainment products and services are created affect demand for, the revenue we can generate from and the cost of producing or distributing our entertainment offerings and our results of operations.
label: de_escalated
evidence: Initially, our DTC streaming services experienced significant losses.
reason: DTC losses are now framed as an initial-period issue rather than ongoing since launch, and the explicit hit to DTC profitability from content cost allocation was dropped.

title: Contentmoderation:
label: escalated
evidence: new regulations apply to online child safety, including access and content restrictions as well as other limitations for minors
reason: Child-safety regulation moves from something legislators are focusing on to rules already in effect, adding access restrictions, so the exposure is now materialising rather than prospective.

title: Failure to successfully execute our omnichannel strategy and the cost of our investments in eCommerce and technology may materially adversely affect our market position, net sales and financial performance.
label: new_exposure
evidence: the increasing role of AI-enabled platforms in product search, discovery, advertising and purchasing
reason: This year adds AI-enabled and agentic third-party shopping platforms as a new driver of store-traffic loss and disintermediation, which last year's text did not address.

title: We may be unable to effectively manage our liquidity, which could adversely affect our business, financial position and results of operations.
label: de_escalated
evidence: we expect negative operating cash flows to continue in future quarters as we work to ramp up commercial airplanes production
reason: This year drops the expectation of continued negative operating cash flow and the pending Spirit net debt, and softens 'further downgrades' to 'downgrades'. Debt levels are roughly unchanged.

title: The performance of strategic alliances and other business relationships to support the expansion of our business could materially adversely affect our financial performance.
label: boilerplate
evidence: These arrangements may not generate the level of sales or profitability we anticipate
reason: Only the parenthetical example of ONE, the fintech venture, was dropped; the company does not say the exposure shrank or ended, so the change is not material.

title: The growth of electronic trading and the introduction of new products and technologies, including trading and distributed ledger technologies, such as cryptocurrencies, and AI technologies, has increased competition.
label: boilerplate
evidence: including stablecoins, digital assets and others based on distributed ledgers
reason: Stablecoins and the firm's own ATS are new examples of already-covered disintermediation and competition risks, with no sign they are materialising or growing.

title: Our products are subject to risks associated with overseas sourcing, manufacturing and financing.
label: boilerplate
evidence: other changes in labor standards and sustainability-related requirements
reason: Adding sustainability requirements and compliance wording only extends regulatory and labor-standard exposures already covered; condensing the materials list into a cross-reference is not substantive.

title: We could be subject to changes in tax rates, the adoption of new US or international tax legislation, or exposure to additional tax liabilities.
label: de_escalated
evidence: the OECD announced a "Side-by-Side Safe Harbor" that exempts US operations of US-parented companies from global minimum tax rules
reason: The new OECD safe harbor exempts the company's US operations from global minimum tax rules, narrowing the Pillar Two exposure to operations outside the US.

title: Our operations could be adversely affected by events outside of our control, such as natural disasters, wars or health epidemics.
label: boilerplate
evidence: geopolitical conflicts impact our ability to access certain facilities or supply chain
reason: The specific Russia-Ukraine passage was swapped for generic geopolitical-conflict language. Wars and conflict disruption were already covered, so the substance is unchanged.

title: The market for prime real estate is competitive.
label: new_exposure
evidence: Declines in store traffic, changes in consumer shopping behavior, shifts to digital commerce, local safety concerns
reason: The company adds new causes of loss that last year's text did not cover: falling store traffic, shifts to digital commerce and local safety concerns affecting store strategy and leases.

title: JPMorganChase could suffer losses if the value of collateral declines.
label: new_exposure
evidence: borrowers may under-maintain or misrepresent the condition or existence of collateral, or at liquidation, collateral could be subject to competing claims
reason: Adds borrower misrepresentation of collateral and competing claims at liquidation, new loss sources beyond the stress-driven valuation risk covered last year, and drops the stressed-conditions limit from the title.

title: Competition.
label: boilerplate
evidence: Technology and expertise provided by industry service companies or AI may also enhance the competitiveness
reason: Adding AI, supranational objectives and divergent energy-transition views only adds examples to competition and reputation risks already covered, without showing the risk growing or materialising.

title: The Company’s operations and performance depend significantly on global and regional economic conditions.
label: boilerplate
evidence: The Company’s operations and performance depend significantly on global and regional economic conditions.
reason: Title shortened, a sentence removed and list reordered; the exposures, examples and impacts described are substantively unchanged.

title: The Company is exposed to the risk of write-downs on the value of its inventory and other assets, in addition to purchase commitment cancellation risk.
label: boilerplate
evidence: Manufacturing purchase obligations cover the Company’s forecasted component and manufacturing requirements.
reason: Only the "typically for periods up to 150 days" detail and "for its products" were removed; the exposure itself is unchanged.

title: Acquisitions, joint ventures, investments, and divestitures could result in operating difficulties, dilution, and other consequences that could harm our business, financial condition, and operating results.
label: escalated
evidence: result in the payment of fees or penalties to a counterparty
reason: The regulatory-approval risk now carries an added monetary cost, likely a deal break fee. The text also adds the risk of failing to find buyers for intended divestitures.

title: We face risks related to changes in our business strategies and plans, which have affected and may continue to affect our cost structure, the value of our assets and/or our results of operations.
label: escalated
evidence: impaired the value of certain of our retail store assets and certain hotel experiences assets
reason: The strategy-change risk is the same, but the company adds a new realized write-down of hotel experiences assets and large new deals (Fubo, NFL/ESPN), showing the risk materialising.
